newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says owed $148 mln in cash calls by Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Shell says owed $148 mln in cash calls by Nigeria.

text.p: Nigeria is indebted to Shell Nigeria to the tune of $148 million in cash call payments, the company's chief executive said on Monday.

Cash calls are Nigeria's share of the funding for its joint ventures with multinational oil firms that explore and produce Nigeria's crude oil. Nigeria has perpetually been in arrears in its contributions to the fund.
"The government is still owing Shell $148 million cash call arrears for 1996," Brian Anderson, the outgoing managing director of Shell Nigeria told a news briefing in Lagos.
In all, the Nigerian government is in arrears of about $1.2 billion in the payment of cash calls to all its six joint venture partners.
"We still need to sort out the 1996 arrears but so far discussions are yet to bring any resolution," Anderson said.
He said Nigeria has been paying its part of the funds for oil operations for this year but what was paid fell short of industry requirement.
"We have been receiving regular payment for 1997 but this is based on a 40 percent cut in our budget," Anderson said.
Nigeria had budgeted $2.05 billion for funding the oil industry this year compared with $3.32 billion which the oil firms had proposed.
"We need to see higher budget allocation in 1997 if the industry is to grow," said Anderson.
He said Shell would begin drilling for oil from its acreage in the Gongola basin in the north by the end of the year.
The company, he said, would also start production from its deep offshore field before the end of the century.
